problem.title_en: How many colors are needed to color the positive integers so that a prescribed integer is not a monochromatic subset sum?

posed.citation: Erdős, P., Graham, R. L. Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Monogr. Enseign. Math. 28 (1980).

items.citation:
# Citation

Candidate under formal verification; review pending.

## English

Erdős Problem JSP-000298 (Erdős Problem #360) investigates the minimum number of colors $f(n)$ required to color the integers $\{1, \dots, n-1\}$ such that no monochromatic subset sums to $n$. Originally posed by Erdős and Graham (1980), bounds of order $n^{1/3 \pm o(1)}$ were established by Noga Alon and Paul Erdős (*Acta Arithmetica* 74(3), 1996, pp. 269–272), with further sharp order bounds established by Conlon, Fox, and Pham (2021).

This machine-checked Lean 4 formalization proves both the elementary cubic-root bound and the general sieve-remainder upper bound theorem from Alon–Erdős (1996, Section 2):
1. **Sieve-Remainder Bound**: For any $n \ge 2, s \ge 1$, and finite set $P$ with elements not dividing $n$, there exists an explicit monochromatic subset-sum-avoiding coloring using $s + |P| + \lceil |R| / s \rceil$ colors (`exists_coloring_sieve`, `minColors_le_sieve`), where $R = \{x \in \{1, \dots, n-1\} \mid (s+1)x < n \wedge \forall p \in P, p \nmid x\}$. Crucially, this combinatorial theorem does not require $n \le s^3$.
2. **Cubic-Root Baseline**: For any $n \le s^3$, an explicit $2s$-coloring avoids monochromatic subset sums (`exists_coloring_of_le_cube`, `minColors_le_two_mul_s`), yielding $f(n) \le 2\lceil n^{1/3}\rceil$.
3. **Covering Principle & Avoidance Blocks**: General covering theorem (`exists_coloring_of_avoiding_family`), interval blocks for any $k \ge 1$ (`interval_block_avoids_subset_sum`), modular divisibility avoidance (`dvd_subset_sum_free`), and small-cardinality blocks (`small_card_block_avoids_subset_sum`).
4. **Lower Bound**: $f(n) \ge 2$ for all $n \ge 3$ (`minColors_ge_two`).
items.recipients:
# Recipients

## English

Attribution for this formal candidate distinguishes the original mathematical proof from the machine-checked Lean 4 formalization:

1. RECIPIENT-JSP-000298-ALON: Noga Alon, co-author of the original mathematical proof establishing upper and lower bounds for monochromatic subset sum colorings (*Acta Arith.* 74 (1996), 269–272).
2. RECIPIENT-JSP-000298-ERDOS: Paul Erdős, who originally posed the problem and co-authored the 1996 resolution.
3. RECIPIENT-JSP-000298-SIXTIMENIGHT: Sixtimenight, author of the original machine-checked Lean 4 formalization, definitions, and verification package.

Formal proof authored by Sixtimenight. Candidate packaging and verification recorded by community curators and verifiers.

statement.text:
theorem exists_coloring_sieve (n s : ℕ) (P : Finset ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hs : 1 ≤ s) (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, ¬ p ∣ n) :
    ∃ c : ℕ → Fin (s + P.card + ((Erdos298.sieveRemainder n s P).card + s - 1) / s),
      Erdos298.AvoidsMonoSubsetSum n (s + P.card + ((Erdos298.sieveRemainder n s P).card + s - 1) / s) c
statement.natural_language_source: Erdos Problem JSP-000298 (Erdos #360, Alon-Erdos 1996, Section 2): Let n >= 2, s >= 1. For any finite set P of elements not dividing n (e.g. primes p <= s with p ∤ n), there exists a coloring of {1, ..., n-1} with s + |P| + ceil(|R|/s) colors avoiding monochromatic subset sums to n, where R = {x in {1, ..., n-1} | (s+1)x < n and for all p in P, p ∤ x}. This combinatorial theorem does not require n <= s^3 and provides the foundation for the logarithmic improvement via prime sieving.

definitions_reviewed.name: Erdos298.HasSubsetSum
definitions_reviewed.review: Specifies existence of a subfinset T ⊆ S with sum equal to target n.

definitions_reviewed.name: Erdos298.AvoidsSubsetSum
definitions_reviewed.review: Negation of HasSubsetSum, asserting that no subfinset of S has sum equal to n.

definitions_reviewed.name: Erdos298.AvoidsMonoSubsetSum
definitions_reviewed.review: Asserts that every color class of coloring c on {1, ..., n-1} avoids subset sum n.

definitions_reviewed.name: Erdos298.intervalBlock
definitions_reviewed.review: Defines the large interval blocks A_k = {x ∈ {1, ..., n-1} | n ≤ (k+1)*x ∧ k*x < n}.

definitions_reviewed.name: Erdos298.sieveRemainder
definitions_reviewed.review: Defines the sieved remainder set R = {x ∈ {1, ..., n-1} | (s+1)*x < n ∧ ∀ p ∈ P, ¬ p ∣ x}.

definitions_reviewed.name: Erdos298.sieveBlock
definitions_reviewed.review: Partitions remainder R into blocks of size at most s by enumerated index: C_j = ((R.toList.drop (j*s)).take s).toFinset.
